name: Lake Elune'ara
summary: Lake Elune'ara is the shimmering, sacred body of water that occupies the heart of Moonglade. Revering the Moon Goddess Elune, the lake serves as a place of spiritual reflection for the Cenarion Circle, though deep within its murky floor lies the dormant, corrupted demigod Omen.

sections.title: Heart of the Sacred Vale
sections.body: Framed by the moonlit groves of Moonglade, Lake Elune'ara provides serene waters said to be blessed by the White Lady herself. The lake lies at the spiritual center of the druidic haven, bordered by Nighthaven to the north and the shrine grounds of the Cenarion Circle. Initiates have long plumbed its tranquil depths to retrieve long-lost relics, attuning themselves to the currents of nature as they seek harmony with the land.

sections.title: The Slumber of Omen
sections.body: Despite the tranquility on the surface, ancient peril rests beneath the gentle ripples. Centuried legends speak of the two-headed wolf demigod Omen, a revered ancient corrupted by the Burning Legion during the War of the Ancients. Defeated and cast into the lake bed long ago, Omen slumbers deep below the dark waters, an enduring reminder of nature's wounds.

faq.answer: It is the large, sacred lake dominating the center of Moonglade. Revered by night elves and druids, it is named after the Moon Goddess Elune and surrounded by the sanctuaries of the Cenarion Circle.

faq.q: What lurks at the bottom of the lake?
faq.answer: The fallen demigod Omen sleeps in the dark depths of the lake. Once a noble ancient, he was driven mad by the Burning Legion during the ancient war and cast into the lake upon his defeat.

faq.q: Why do druids come to this lake?
faq.answer: The lake is deeply connected to druidic trials and communing with the spirits of nature. Young druids often delve into its waters searching for sacred relics as part of their rites of passage.

angles.text: The lake is an integral site for druidic rituals and testing, holding sacred relics within its deep waters that aid initiates on their path.
Named for Elune, the lake represents a place of divine peace and historical memory of the War of the Ancients.
